review.disposition: Query and static header grammar approved; initial runtime header acceptance withheld before the raw adapter was implemented.

implemented: Named closed-Object query binding and anonymous explicitly mapped header binding syntax.
Cross-boundary binding collision, header wire-name, scalar-type and protected-header checks.
Scalar Object defaults including PageSize default 25.
Strict raw percent/UTF-8 validation, one form-decoding pass, duplicate and unknown query rejection.
Structured query JSON decoding with 400 syntax versus 422 typed-value failures.
Query inventory, validator-plan and OpenAPI derivation.
Built-in node:http adapter that counts IncomingMessage.rawHeaders before Fetch Request construction and rejects duplicate declared headers.
Streaming node:http request-body conversion so authentication and CSRF checks run before body consumption, with unconsumed input resumed after the response.
Safe-integer rejection for typed Int query values before lossy JavaScript number conversion can be accepted.

focused_runtime.protected_boundary: Missing and valid bearer credentials, wrong and valid browser Origin/CSRF, duplicate raw Authorization lines, streamed POST body conversion, response delivery, and no extra writes.

header_probe.ordinary_duplicate: Repeated mixed-case X-Trace lines were exposed as only the final value, indistinguishable from one header.
header_probe.get_all: Headers.getAll throws for names other than set-cookie.
header_probe.authorization_comparison: Authorization duplicates coalesce, so that separate probe does not establish ordinary-header multiplicity.
header_probe.conclusion: The Fetch Request boundary cannot implement duplicate rejection alone; Bun's built-in node:http IncomingMessage.rawHeaders preserves both lines for a generated pre-Fetch adapter.

final_runtime_review.disposition: The streaming adapter and safe-integer check resolve both findings; protected real-listener authentication and CSRF parity is established.

supported_verification.remaining_scope: The complete frozen golden application and release gates remain owned by RM-109/RM-110.
